supporterLens.note: Round 1: YES with a non-blocking placement finding -- the refresh's structural fact closed the OPPONENTS' paragraph, so that side ended on two procedural sentences while supporters ended on an argument. ACCEPTED; the fact moved to its own neutral h3. Also verified there is NO stored on-record Roy/Lee/Cornyn statement about this development (the only stored explanation of the mechanism, Speaker Johnson's, is about the FAILED June 30 rule, a different resolution), so nothing was added -- omitted rather than softened-and-kept. Round 2: YES; flagged the terminal "neither..." clause as a yes-but cadence and proposed a positive rewrite, which was adopted and then superseded (see opponentLens round 3). Round 3: YES on the shipped wording; argued for KEEPING "Section 11 included" on supporter-protective grounds -- without it the closing quantifier is easy to misread as "the text was never voted on at all", which is false and under-credits the result.

opponentLens.note: Round 1: NO -- BLOCKING. The clause "were recorded on the rule and on the defense bill" added no fact and only reclassified the two votes as unremarkable; as the last words of the opponents' paragraph it read as a rebuttal-in-advance. Fixed by moving the fact out of that paragraph and stating the absence of a dedicated vote as fact. Round 2: YES; independently confirmed the opponents' paragraph is byte-identical to the pre-refresh live article, and re-confirmed as a settled call that the stored McGovern ("shell game", "zero percent chance") and Jeffries quotes CANNOT be used here without misstating the timeline -- both react to the failed June 30 rule, not to H. Res. 1438; they belong to the ndaa-fy2027 article, which holds those reporting sources. Round 3: NO on the supporter's positive rewrite, on grammar rather than politics -- a trailing "rather than X" binds to the nearest clause, so its scope over BOTH votes became ambiguous where "neither... was" is an explicit quantifier, and the same edit promoted one half of a fact pair to an independent clause while demoting the other to a trailing phrase. Proposed a merge keeping both; that merge is what ships, verbatim.

bothSidesReview.residualDisagreement: RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED (2026-08-27): the two lenses converged on accuracy and both signed off on the shipped sentence, but they still differ on EMPHASIS. The supporter reviewer would reorder it so the section does not end on the "neither was a separate vote" quantifier; the opponent reviewer signed off specifically because that quantifier holds terminal, independent-clause position with unambiguous scope. Each called the other's preference non-blocking. The reorder was NOT applied: it would reopen the opponent's round-3 scope-and-weight test, and trading one lens's non-blocking preference for the other's is churn, not convergence. resolution:
Retrofit of a pre-lane both-sides tracker (published 2026-07-17 with linked-not-stored sources and no ledger). Every named position fetched and STORED (11 primary sources: 2 bill texts, 3 Congress.gov records, 1 House roll-call record, 5 org/member statements). 11 findings fixed: 2 material omissions (unsourced 80% popularity claim; unsourced attestation-baseline contrast) removed per Sec 6.4; 9 minor.
